newsitem.title: UK: Shell confident of Italy LNG deal,eyes Asia growth.
newsitem.headline: Shell confident of Italy LNG deal,eyes Asia growth.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell Group is confident an agreement will be reached with Italy over a gas purchase contract and Shell does not have to look for alternative buyers, Shell Chairman John Jennings said on Thursday.
The Far East presented the greatest opportunity for future liquefied natural gas (LNG) markets, he said.

"I believe ways will be found for delivery under the terms of that contract," Jennings told a briefing after Shell announced its 1996 earnings. "I still don't necessarily see that we have to find alternatives."
Enel, the Italian state power company, pulled out of a contract in December to buy 3.5 billion cubic metres of gas per year from Nigeria.
Nigeria and Italy have been in talks aimed at reaching an amicable out-of-court settlement over the cancellation, Nigeria's oil minister Dan Etete said on Sunday.
Shell is the technical leader for the $4 billion LNG plant that is expected to produce 7.2 billion cubic metres of gas per year from 1999.
"We have a clear firm contract with Enel and we're trying to find ways to ensure that contract is fulfilled," he said.
"It may be that phasing in of the volumes to Italy will have to be looked at, but that would be almost a detail."
In Asia, new markets were opening up in Korea, Taiwan, Thailand, China and India, while increased production from the Middle East would help meet that demand, he said.
"The Atlantic (Basin) LNG (market) is in a very early stage and I'm sure it will become important. The Far East LNG is much more mature and set to continue to grow," he said.
He said Brazil was a potential new Atlantic Basin market to complement Northwest Europe and the eastern United States.
